newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee futures rally falters after brief run.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee futures rally falters after brief run.

text.p: London coffee futures jumped late on Wednesday afternoon fuelled by New York's steep rise on a report, later said to have been based on an erroneous calculation, that the Colombia National Coffee Growers' Federation cut its 1996/97 crop estimates to 8.3 million bags.

After the London close, the Federation reiterated that its earlier forecast of 10.4 million bags, made last week, still stands. A spokesman said the new, lower forecast had been based on an erroneous calculation.
By the close the London May robusta contract was $35 firmer at $1,580 after racing by nearly five percent to a peak of $1,620.

The prices stepped back from the ceiling after the London-based Economist Intelligence Unit revised upward its forecast of the world 1997/98 crop surplus to 4.0 million bags from 1.9 million previously.
Volume was 9,528 lots, dominated by the three front months March, May and July.
A spokesman at the Colombia's National Coffee Growers' Federation said the new, low forecast it gave out was erroneous.
"The calculation was wrong," said Romn Medina, explaining that he failed to take into account 2 million bags of January to March production.
He said production for the coffee year was still seen at a level of about 10.4 million bags, down from 12.9 million in the 1995/96 coffee year.
London prices had held some $20-$30 gain in quiet morning dealings on further trade buying as overnight selling by origins and funds dried up.
The sustained trade buying followed perception that prices had found an immediate bottom at just above $1,500 basis May.
"People who were starting to turn a bit bearish now realised that there's very little room for the market to go lower," a trader said earlier in the day.
The EIU put world 1997/98 coffee surplus at 4.0 million 60-kg bags, up from its earlier estimate of 1.9 million, and compared with a 2.0 million surplus in the current 1996/97 season.

It kept its world 1997/98 consumption estimate largely unchanged at 75.7 million but it revised upward exportable production figure to 79.7 million from 77.5 million previously on expectations of larger robusta supplies especially from Ivory Coast and Vietnam.
Coffee experienced a supply deficit of 7.6 million in 1995/96. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
